subject: Social Habits
title: Road and street safety
objectives: Children will hold an adult’s hand near roads.
Children will stop at a pretend kerb and look and listen.
content: Holding hands near roads, stop, look and listen, and safe walking.
teachingActivities: Always practise in a safe, closed play space with chalk roads and toy cars; never practise on a real road with children as the lesson; stress holding an adult’s hand; use short rules; link to what families do on the way to school; invite parents to hold hands at the gate.
learnerActivities: Hold an adult’s hand near roads and stop, look and listen at a pretend kerb.
assessment: Observe whether each child holds a hand to walk and stops at a pretend kerb on request.
expectedOutcomes: Holds an adult’s hand to walk.
Stops at a pretend kerb on request.

lessons.title: Holding hands near roads
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will hold an adult’s hand when walking near roads.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have learnt safety at school and know community helpers.
lessons.starter: Draw a chalk road and say "Roads are for cars. Children hold a grown-up’s hand."
teacherActivities: Show how to hold an adult’s hand firmly.
Walk beside the chalk road holding hands.
Stop and start with hands held.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show how to hold an adult’s hand firmly. Children: Children hold a partner’s hand.
Step 2. Teacher: Walk beside the chalk road holding hands. Children: Children walk with a partner.
Step 3. Teacher: Say "Always hold hands near roads." Children: Children repeat hold hands.
Step 4. Teacher: Stop and start with hands held. Children: Children stop and wait.

practical.title: Hold hands on the road
practical.safety: Practise only in a closed safe area, never on a real road. An adult must hold every child’s hand.

differentiation.support: Hold the child’s hand and walk together.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to tell a friend to hold hands.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What do we hold near roads?
Are roads safe to run on?

lessons.homeConnection: Hold your child’s hand firmly near roads and say "Hold hands."
teacherReflection: Which children could show "hold an adult’s hand when walking near roads" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

learnerFacing.songOrRhyme: Hold my hand, hold my hand, when we walk on the road.

lessons.title: Stop, look and listen
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will stop, look and listen at a pretend kerb.
successCriteria: Looks and listens with an adult
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have learnt safety at school and know community helpers.
resources: A line of tape as a kerb
lessons.starter: Put a tape line on the floor and say "This is the kerb. We stop at the kerb."
teacherActivities: Show how to stop at the kerb, look and listen.
Play a car sound and say "A car is coming. Wait."
Say "When it is safe, we walk with a grown-up."
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show how to stop at the kerb, look and listen. Children: Children watch and copy.
Step 2. Teacher: Play a car sound and say "A car is coming. Wait." Children: Children wait at the line.
Step 3. Teacher: Say "When it is safe, we walk with a grown-up." Children: Children hold hands.
Step 4. Teacher: Practise again with each child. Children: Child stops and looks.

practical.title: Stop at the kerb
practical.safety: Use a floor line only and never use a real road. Supervise every child and hold hands for each crossing.

differentiation.support: Stand at the line and look together.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to be the traffic helper.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What do we do at the kerb?

expectedOutcomes: Looks and listens with an adult
lessons.homeConnection: Practise stop, look and listen when you walk with your child.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "stop, look and listen at a pretend kerb" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Safe walking
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will practise walking safely in a line with an adult.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have learnt safety at school and know community helpers.
resources: A hat or bag to carry
lessons.starter: Draw a chalk pavement and road and say "We walk on the pavement, not the road."
teacherActivities: Show the pavement and the road.
Walk along the pavement with a partner.
Stop at the corner and look both ways.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show the pavement and the road. Children: Children look and point.
Step 2. Teacher: Walk along the pavement with a partner. Children: Children walk in pairs.
Step 3. Teacher: Stop at the corner and look both ways. Children: Children stop and look.
Step 4. Teacher: Say "Safe walking." Children: Children repeat safe walking.

practical.title: Pavement walk
practical.safety: Use chalk lines in a closed area only and keep an adult beside each pair. Never practise near real traffic.

differentiation.support: Walk with the child holding hands.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to lead a pair along the pavement.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What do we do at the corner?

lessons.conclusion: Walk back together and wave goodbye.
lessons.homeConnection: Walk on the pavement together and talk about safety.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "practise walking safely in a line with an adult" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Traffic play
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will play a traffic game that uses stop and go.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have learnt safety at school and know community helpers.
resources: A stop sign and a go sign
lessons.starter: Give out paper plate steering wheels and say "Today we are drivers. Stop when I show stop."
teacherActivities: Show the stop and go signs and say what each means.
Let children drive around the chalk road.
Change the signs quickly and slowly.
Let each child hold the sign.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show the stop and go signs and say what each means. Children: Children look and repeat.
Step 2. Teacher: Let children drive around the chalk road. Children: Children drive and stop.
Step 3. Teacher: Change the signs quickly and slowly. Children: Children stop and go.
Step 4. Teacher: Let each child hold the sign. Children: Child shows the sign.

practical.title: Drivers on the road
steps: Go when the sign says go.
practical.safety: Keep speeds slow and the area clear. Stop the game if children run into each other.

differentiation.support: Drive beside the child and show the signs.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to be the road helper with the signs.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What do we do at stop?
What do we do at go?

expectedOutcomes: Takes a turn as the driver
lessons.conclusion: Park the cars and say well done.
lessons.homeConnection: Play stop and go games at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "play a traffic game that uses stop and go" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Week 5 road safety check
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Teachers will observe how each child follows road safety rules.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have learnt safety at school and know community helpers.
lessons.starter: Sing the road safety song and show three stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: hold hands, kerb and traffic game.
At each station watch how the child follows the rule.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: hold hands, kerb and traffic game. Children: Children rotate every four minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station watch how the child follows the rule. Children: Child follows with a prompt.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Road safety stations
practical.safety: Supervise each station and use a closed safe area only. Never practise on real roads.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and use one station.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to remind a friend.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: holds an adult’s hand; stops at a kerb; looks and listens; walks safely.

questions.question: What do we hold near roads?
What do we do at the kerb?

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 5
Follows road safety rules with support
lessons.conclusion: Wave goodbye and say stay safe.
lessons.homeConnection: Keep practising road safety with your child.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will observe how each child follows road safety rules" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
